correctness.rationale: The exact model axioms imply p=g∘q_Λ for a strictly increasing g, so a cross-part unlike-color exchange is beneficial exactly according to the sign of (1/2−Λ)(1/2−t). All other swaps cannot strictly benefit both. This yields one-dimensional transitions x→x±1, the complete three-regime equilibrium set, and a potential clock reduced by one on every profitable swap. Binomial counting, a verified telescoping identity, and Stirling give the exact equilibrium counts and expected lengths. The standalone rational checker exhaustively tested 32,928 initial state/peak instances, 215,664 profitable pairs, and exact D_n for n=2..12. Finite verification does not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The main 2022 source establishes general existence and finite-improvement conditions but does not say how drastically the entire equilibrium landscape changes at tolerance one half. The complete three-regime counting theorem and exact choice-independent strict-swap lengths quantitatively describe this standard social network game on every balanced biclique. Hypergeometric initialization reveals a linear-to-square-root mean path-length change. This is a natural structural classification, not an arbitrary finite sample.
